**Question 1:** What causes a React component to re-render?

turns.text: Sure. A React component re-renders mainly when its state changes via setState or a useState setter, when its parent re-renders (by default children re-render too, even if props didn't change, unless you wrap them in React.memo), or when a context it consumes with useContext gets a new value. Also custom hooks that use state internally will trigger it. Worth noting a re-render doesn't always mean a DOM update, React diffs the virtual DOM and only commits what changed. To cut down unnecessary renders you can use React.memo, useMemo/useCallback for stable references, and keep state as local as possible.

Thanks, Sana. That's a clear and thorough answer.

**Question 2:** Explain the event loop in one minute.
